approach: Three small edits in two source files plus tests, no new file, interface, dependency or language change. (1) render.ts pageHtml: add the bare tag `<script src="/api/packages/story.js"></script>` on its own line immediately BEFORE the bundle script and AFTER the data-block script. That keeps the bundle script last, so the existing `indexOf('<script>')` / `lastIndexOf('</script>')` slices in render.test.ts:96 and :146 still land on the bundle (the helper tag carries an attribute so indexOf('<script>') skips it), and client.tsx still finds #page-data before it runs. The shell has no timestamp or nonce, so bytes stay deterministic (GROUND probed `cmp` identical today). The spelling is the contract's: selector-contract.md Settled row. (2) app.tsx Declaration (line 1468): add `data-declaration={...}` to `<section className="d-decl">` using the `body.id` already in hand there, set only when it is a string (when it is absent or not a string the component already draws a 'no id' Err, so no attribute is emitted for that card). React escapes attribute values, so no new escaper is needed and render.ts's &/< escapeHtml (unsafe for attributes) is not touched; quotes and punctuation in an id are escaped by React's renderer. (3) app.tsx Table (line 719): give each member `<tr>` a `data-member` value derived from the shape being tabulated, not from a column called `name`. Reuse existing owners and add nothing: `propertiesOf(bodyOf, of)` already supplies the columns, and `derivesFrom(bodyOf, type, 'name')` (words.ts:555, the same question syntax.ts:294 already asks) plus `typeOfProperty` (words.ts:436) pick the column whose declared type is MetaLang's `name`. For arch's `member` this finds `name` (is: name) with NO change to arch.yaml, which avoids the language change the selector contract says needs its own approval. Reuse the ledger's owner `propertyCarrying` (words.ts:422, role name) first where a shape declares `role: name`, and fall back to the type-is-name column, so there is one resolver, not two. The 'name' type word is the one constant syntax.ts:111 keeps private; move/export that single constant from words.ts next to SELF rather than writing the literal a second time (DRY). If zero or several columns qualify the row carries no data-member (the shape has no single name), mirroring propertyCarrying's documented 'answers none draws as before', and a beat aimed at it is reported as a missing target by the helper; this is flagged for Tim below because CLAUDE.md rule 1 forbids a silent 'could not tell'. (4) Missing / ambiguous target reporting is the JARVIS helper's job at beat time; in this repo the loud part is a render-time proof: tests assert the model document yields exactly one match for each intended selector and zero matches for a name that does not exist, and nothing in the renderer widens a selector. (5) Tests, RED first: render.test.ts asserts the helper tag exists exactly once, sits after #page-data and before the bundle, and two renders of the same input are byte-identical; app.test.tsx asserts data-declaration on each card, data-member on each row, a member name repeated across two declarations resolves to one match when scoped by declaration, an id with quotes, `<`, `&`, `]` round-trips as an attribute value, and existing data-part / data-col targets unchanged. A kit.test.ts case renders under plain node and checks the tag and attributes appear from a built kit. (6) Release is the existing kit-release controls (pinned version, commit sha, asset SHA-256, download URL to Diagnostics per selector-contract.md); no new mechanism. propose.ts's separate page is left alone because the issue names only pageHtml.

approach:
Build each of the issue's needs as one general seam with one owner, verified against the live tree.

1. STORY HELPER (render.ts, pageHtml, the sole shell producer, render.ts:60-72). Add one exported constant STORY_HELPER_SRC = '/api/packages/story.js' and emit `<script src="${STORY_HELPER_SRC}"></script>` as a constant tag with no variable input. Place it after `<main id="root">` and before the page-data block and the bundle. This keeps the data block ahead of the bundle (client.tsx:15-16 throws otherwise). The bundle stays the last script, and the tag carries an attribute, so render.test.ts:96 and :146 (`indexOf('<script>')` and `lastIndexOf('</script>')`) still slice only the bundle. Both the repo `render` command and the kit go through pageHtml, so one change reaches both after a kit rebuild. propose.ts:882 has its own template and is not touched; the issue names only pageHtml.

2. DECLARATION IDENTITY (app.tsx Declaration, section at ~1468). Add `data-declaration={id}` as a JSX prop, so React escapes it. Do not concatenate markup. The id is `body.id` where it is a non-empty string. Where it is missing, the existing 'no id' em and Err band (app.tsx:1485-1498) is the loud report, so the section carries no attribute. Declaration is called from one place (app.tsx:1828) and the section is the only `d-decl` writer, so nothing else needs the id. `data-part` (app.tsx:963) and `data-col` (736, 757) are untouched, and no existing test asserts the section's opening tag.

3. MEMBER IDENTITY (app.tsx Table, ~719-785). Derive the row identity from the rulebook through the existing single owner, `propertyCarrying(bodyOf, of, ROLES.name)` (words.ts:422, ledger verdict: reuse). Compute it once per table beside `columns`, then put `data-member={String(member[nameColumn])}` on the data `<tr>`, not on the `r-note` sibling row. The `<tr>` id and className used for marks are left as they are. No property is named by spelling, so a shape whose identifying column is called anything, or comes in any position, works. The one change in the language: arch.yaml `member.name` (line ~517) gets `role: name`. That is exactly the 'name it is known by' meaning, and the `distinct by role` constraint is satisfied because `kind` and `does` carry other roles. The other consumers of ROLES.name are unaffected: shownBy/calledBy and the Rungs at app.tsx:590 and :683 read enum value types, and propose.ts:379 reads proposal types. I rejected two alternatives. 'The property whose type is `name`' bakes a type's spelling into the renderer (SOLID rail 3). 'First column' breaks on the first shape that declares another column first. When a shape has no ROLES.name property, or two carry it, the rows get no data-member. The silence is closed by the target resolver in step 4, not left standing.

4. EXACTLY-ONE TARGET SEAM (a new small module, ts/metalang/target.ts, with two pure functions). `attributeSelector(attribute, value)` builds a CSS attribute selector with `\` and `"` escaped, so ids with punctuation and quotes round-trip. `soleMatch(html, selector)` returns the single match, and throws a named error on zero matches ('no element matches X') and on more than one ('N elements match X, ambiguous'). It never falls back to a broader selector. The nature of the page (drawn in the browser; the CLI emits an empty `<main>`) means tests run it over renderToStaticMarkup output (app.test.tsx:17-21). The same seam is what a kit command would call. A `node kit.js target <file> <selector>` command is a new public command and a Tim decision. I include it in the design as the known need, flagged for his yes, rather than deferring it.

5. DETERMINISM. No clock, random value or hash enters the shell or the identity code. Identity follows document order (propertiesOf Map order, array index). Add a byte-equality test: render the same document twice through renderWith and compare. Also render through a built kit under node twice, reusing the kit.test.ts:179-205 pattern with arch.yaml. GROUND already probed two builds as identical under Bun 1.2.14.

6. TESTS (RED first). render.test.ts: helper tag is present with the exact literal, appears before the data block and the bundle, and the bundle slice assertions still hold. app.test.tsx: `[data-declaration="IGrantStore"] [data-part="members"]` resolves to exactly one element on a two-declaration fixture. The same member name in two declarations resolves to one row under each declaration's selector. An id containing quotes, brackets and `<` is escaped in the markup and selectable. A shape with no name role gives rows without data-member and a target on it reports 'matches nothing'. Existing data-part and data-col tests (app.test.tsx:990-1110, 1544) pass unchanged. The ledger notes parts.yaml is the only repo document with Table output, so fixtures cover the other shapes.

7. RELEASE. Changing pageHtml and app.tsx changes kit.js and page.js and therefore the digest, so a new kit release through the existing release job (ci.yml:577-599) is the delivery. The four items for the JARVIS lane (tag, 40-char sha, SHA-256 of evolang-kit.zip, download URL) are handed over at release, as selector-contract.md says. Documents checked under the old kit need revalidating and a new revision.

approach:
RISK-FIRST DESIGN — make every corner-cut here either impossible or greppable, and gate the two choices that cannot be defaulted.

TWO DECISIONS FOR TIM BEFORE IMPLEMENT (neither is auto-resolvable; leaving either to the implementer is a rails-decisions "undecided forced choice"):

D1 — how a member's identity is found. My pick: add `role: name` to `member.name` in `ts/metalang/arch.yaml`, and widen the `role: name` doc text in `ts/metalang/metalang.yaml:1011-1018` from the display-name wording to "the name this thing is known by", so the renderer asks the ONE existing owner `propertyCarrying(bodyOf, of, ROLES.name)` (`ts/metalang/words.ts:422`). Why the other two lose: "first column" bakes an observed data pattern into the logic (SOLID rail 3, real-work rail 3) and dies on the first shape that declares something else first — the test-only `equivalent` entity at `app.test.tsx:1070-1110` is already such a shape. "Find the property whose declared type is MetaLang's `name`" creates a SECOND answer to the question `propertiesCarrying` already owns, against its own doc comment ("This is the one place the question 'which property of this type carries that role' is answered") — SOLID rails 1 and 4. Cost of my pick is a language-file change, which `selector-contract.md` says "changes the language and needs its own approval". I verified it is drawing-safe: all three `ROLES.name` consumers (`app.tsx:590` shownBy, `app.tsx:683` Rungs, `propose.ts:379`) reach the role only through `typeOfOwnValue` of a closed set, and `member` is used only as `list: { of: member }` (`arch.yaml:582`), never as an enum's value type — so no existing page changes. `distinct: { in: properties, by: role }` stays satisfied (member would carry kind, prose, name). No existing test asserts member has no name role (`words.test.ts:551` asserts only kind).

D2 — what the acceptance resolves targets with. My pick: add ONE pinned DOM devDependency (happy-dom) so the acceptance resolves `[data-declaration=…] [data-member=…]` the way the browser and JARVIS's `story.js` do. Measured reason, not a preference: I probed Bun 1.2.14's built-in HTMLRewriter in this worktree. It resolves plain descendant selectors (1 match, correct), but `getAttribute` returns the RAW entity text (`a"b&c<d>e'f`, not equal to the id) and a selector carrying an escaped value matched 0 elements. React's `renderToStaticMarkup` does escape correctly (`"`→`"`, `&`→`&`, `<`→`<`, `>`→`>`, `'`→`'`). So the no-dependency option silently disagrees with the browser on exactly the "punctuation and quotes in an id" case the issue requires — it would either pass wrongly or get "fixed" by softening the fixture to a plain identifier. A DOM also buys the only honest end-to-end proof: the CLI-rendered page carries an empty `<main id="root">` and nothing resolves until the bundle runs, so a DOM is what proves the BUILT `page.js` carries the change.

THE BUILD, once those are answered:

1. Shell. `pageHtml` (`render.ts:60-72`) emits the settled tag verbatim — `<script src="/api/packages/story.js"></script>` — as a constant with no interpolation, placed LAST, after the bundle script, before `</html>`. Last is the only position that cannot block the page when the helper 404s outside JARVIS (the shell has no `<head>`/`<body>`, and an external classic script earlier blocks the parse until the fetch fails), and it gives the helper a mounted DOM. Pin the whole shell with a byte-exact assertion, not `toContain`, so the position is locked rather than remembered.

2. Declaration identity. In `Declaration` (`app.tsx:1468`), the section takes `data-declaration={body.id}` under the SAME predicate already written at `app.tsx:1485` (`typeof body.id === 'string' && body.id.length > 0`), extracted to one named const consumed by both the `d-id` span and the attribute so the two cannot drift (DRY rail 5). No id → no attribute; the existing `no id` em and the `Err` at `app.tsx:1502` already report it. Value goes through JSX, so React escapes it and no escaper is written.

3. Member identity. `Table` (`app.tsx:719-785`) asks `propertyCarrying(bodyOf, of, ROLES.name)` ONCE per table, above the row map. Each data `<tr>` takes `data-member={text(member[part])}` when that yields a non-empty string; the `tr.r-note` sibling (`app.tsx:773-779`) never does, and the existing `className`/`id` mark attributes are untouched. Zero carriers → no attribute, no error, which is the owner's stated contract ("A thing whose type answers none of the three draws as it drew before the language had the word", `words.ts:425-428`). Two carriers → `propertyCarrying` returns undefined, so again no attribute, and NOTHING NEW is written to report it: the page's existing `Err` at `app.tsx:1088-1093` already names both carriers, and the checker already faults it through `distinct: { in: properties, by: role }`. Loudness is reused, not reinvented.

4. One target-resolution owner, test-scope. A single helper every selector assertion goes through: resolve(html, selector) → exactly-one / missing(selector) / ambiguous(count). It never substitutes a broader selector; missing and ambiguous both fail loudly naming the selector and the count (CLAUDE.md rule 1, guide 5a). It stays test-scope because the approved plan's words for this lane are "Add the existing story helper to the kit renderer; add stable declaration and member identities; preserve section and column targets" — shipping a `kit.js targets` command would be unapproved scope, and the runtime report-don't-widen behaviour is the JARVIS half (4thWAIV/jarvis#120).

5. Acceptance, all in the existing test files. (a) The real in-repo document `ts/metalang/parts.yaml` — 7 declarations, 4 member tables, 18 member rows: every declaration id resolves to exactly one section, every `[data-declaration="X"] [data-part="members"]` to exactly one, every member row by name inside its own declaration. (b) An inline fixture declaring its OWN entity with `role: name` against a language that is not arch, proving the mechanism is language-agnostic and not an arch special case (real-work rail 3). (c) A repeated member name across two declarations — `parts.yaml` has 18 distinct names, so this case needs the inline fixture; each target resolves to exactly one. (d) An id carrying `"`, `'`, `&`, `<`, `>`: assert the DECODED attribute value equals the id exactly and that the escaped selector resolves to one — never a substring assertion. (e) Duplicate declaration ids → resolver reports ambiguous, and the checker already faults it (`check.ts:1005`). (f) A shape with no name role → no `data-member`, resolver reports missing. (g) Every existing `data-part`/`data-col` byte assertion (`app.test.tsx:1098-1110`, `:1544`) and the marked-row id assertion (`:1559`) pass untouched. (h) Byte identity, which does not exist today: one document rendered twice compared byte for byte, and two kit builds compared per-file. (i) Through the built kit: `node kit.js render` output carries the helper tag, and the built `page.js` executed in the DOM yields the same resolved targets as the component render — the proof that what JARVIS downloads carries the change.

6. Release. The change necessarily moves `page.js` and `kit.js`, so the digest changes once; the four Diagnostics facts, the new digest, revalidation of the model surface revision, and immutability of signed packages all run through the existing controls. Rule R7 below closes the live mismatch GROUND found first: the CI release job's non-empty check (`ci.yml:577-599`) omits `style.css` and `syntax.css`, which the consumer requires — a kit released from this branch could be refused at adoption time.

RULE MECHANISM. The TS side has no custom lint rule infrastructure (`eslint.config.js` wires only `@eslint/js` + `typescript-eslint`, no local plugin), and adding a plugin mechanism is a design element that outlives its function. The rules below are therefore contract-directed test rules that scan source and run inside the `bun test` step CI already executes (`ci.yml:437-441`) — the in-repo precedent is `examples.test.ts`, which walks the repository root, and, on the .NET side, `EvidenceUploadsCannotRegressTests.cs`, which reads the workflow file. Each ships with a violating fixture proving it fires and a compliant one proving it does not. If Tim prefers them as ESLint local rules instead, that is his call and the rule content is unchanged.
keySteps: Gate on D1 (role: name on arch.yaml member.name + widen the metalang.yaml role doc text) and D2 (one pinned DOM devDependency for target resolution). Neither can be defaulted; nothing else starts until both are answered.
RULE-PHASE first, under the fence: land R1-R7 with violating and compliant fixtures, so the corner-cuts are impossible or greppable BEFORE any renderer code exists to cut them.
pageHtml: emit the settled story-helper tag verbatim as a constant, last line before </html>, and pin the whole shell byte-exact (not toContain) so its position is locked.
Declaration: extract the existing id predicate at app.tsx:1485 to one named const and feed both the d-id span and a new data-declaration={body.id} JSX attribute from it; no id means no attribute.
Table: ask propertyCarrying(bodyOf, of, ROLES.name) once per table; each data tr takes data-member from that property's text when non-empty; the r-note row never does; mark className/id untouched.
Zero carriers draws no attribute and no error (words.ts:425-428); two carriers reuses the existing Err at app.tsx:1088 and the checker's distinct-by-role fault. Write no new diagnostic.
Build one test-scope target resolver returning exactly-one / missing / ambiguous, and route every selector assertion through it; it never widens a selector.

Acceptance over the real document parts.yaml (7 declarations, 4 tables, 18 rows) plus inline fixtures for a repeated member name, a quoted/punctuated id asserted on the decoded attribute value, duplicate declaration ids, and a shape with no name role.
Add the byte-identity gate that does not exist today: render one document twice and compare bytes; build the kit twice and compare per-file hashes.
Prove it through the built kit: node kit.js render carries the helper tag, and the built page.js executed in the DOM resolves the same targets as the component render.
Fix the CI/carried-file mismatch (ci.yml omits style.css and syntax.css) before the release, under rule R7, then run the release and hand Diagnostics the tag, 40-char sha, asset SHA-256 and URL.
Hand the JARVIS lane the two literal targets to verify there after adoption, with the re-cut revision of the model surface; they cannot be proven in this repository.

risks: The two literal targets cannot be proven in this repository. No MetaLang document here declares IGrantStore or IWindowsHelloNativeOps (grep hits only C# sources and the 114 docs), and .dev/inprocess/106-silent-failure-cleanup/ does not exist in this worktree — the nine-declaration surface lives in the JARVIS document store. In-repo acceptance proves the general property on parts.yaml plus fixtures; the two literal targets are verified on the JARVIS side after the kit release. Writing those two ids into a repo fixture would be the hardcoded-specific cheat and would prove nothing.

Bun's built-in HTMLRewriter cannot be trusted for this acceptance. Measured in this worktree on bun 1.2.14: getAttribute returns raw entity text (a"b&c<d>e'f, not equal to the id) and a selector carrying an escaped value matched 0 elements, while the browser matches. Verification built on it silently passes the quoted-id case the issue requires.

The rendered page's #root is empty — the DOM is drawn in the browser by page.js. A selector test aimed at the CLI output finds zero matches, and the obvious 'fix' is to loosen the assertion. Every target assertion must run against the Page component render (the same root client.tsx mounts) or against the executed bundle.

GROUND's ledger reads as 'reuse propertyCarrying, no new capability', and its evidence cites arch.yaml:211 — but that role: name sits on word.name, not member.name. propertyCarrying(bodyOf, 'member', ROLES.name) returns undefined today. Taken at face value, IMPLEMENT ships a data-member that never appears and the intended target cannot match. This is why D1 is a decision and not a reuse.

story.js belongs to JARVIS and is not readable from this repository, so its load-order expectations are unproven here. Helper-last cannot block the page and gives the helper a mounted DOM, but the JARVIS lane (#120) must confirm the helper tolerates being loaded after React mounts.

The language change means every document checked under the old kit needs revalidating and a new revision; the model surface revision must be re-cut before any beat is written against the new targets, and already-signed packages stay immutable.

Executing the built page.js in a DOM may be slow or flaky. If that leg is dropped, the proof of the BUILT bundle degrades to a string check on page.js — a weaker claim that must be reported as such, never quietly swapped in.
The ts coverage floor is 0.75 (bunfig.toml, matching eng/coverage-gate.sh). New renderer code carries its own tests or the gate fails; lowering the floor or skipping a leg to get green is out.

Duplicate declaration ids are possible (app.test.tsx:100 'one id declared twice keeps the first'), so a target can legitimately match two cards. The issue names only the repeated-member-name case; the duplicate-id case is the one that would silently ring the wrong card, so the acceptance must cover it and the resolver must report ambiguous rather than take the first.
